title: Preregistered next-hypothesis slate
ranking_basis: Planning prior by expected catalogue-proxy holdout improvement per engineering cost and local-data feasibility; ranges are NOT measured or leaderboard predictions.

hypotheses.name: Deformation-seismicity support along persistent basement corridors
hypotheses.signature: Explicit interaction between corrected cross-scale potential-field persistence and coherent geodetic-strain / earthquake-density support, added to a dense head; matched per-quadrant budget.
hypotheses.why_unmapped: A brittle fault can remain active beneath cover without a visible scarp or public Quaternary trace. Joint structural, strain and seismic support is more selective than any raw layer by itself.
hypotheses.difference_from_repo: Persistence-only features and an independent 2 m probe feature arm exist; the sibling DILCOND test used dilatation x conductivity without a worm-selected corridor. No checked-in GEMSDOE29 feature explicitly interacts persistence with strain and earthquake density.
hypotheses.data_availability: Existing hash-pinned owner-mirror feature stack; no new external file. Owner mirror is not organizer-authenticated.
hypotheses.gate: mean paired delta >= +0.005; >=3/4 folds positive on draws 0 and 1, and same threshold on draw 2 or 3; also beat best same-fold/draw pre-existing control

hypotheses.name: Flight-line-frequency notch before magnetic worming
hypotheses.signature: Measure narrow cross-line spectral peaks at frequencies corresponding to officially documented 200/400 m flight-line spacing; only then apply a preregistered notch and recompute the continuation ladder.
hypotheses.why_unmapped: A measured line-periodic acquisition artifact can mask weak basement contacts; removing a verified artifact could expose a fault that is not present in the published surface-trace catalogue.
hypotheses.difference_from_repo: Existing work audits persistence by edge strike but implements no spectral-domain notch. The E-W persistence inversion refutes a simple strike filter, not this frequency-specific test.
hypotheses.data_availability: Local grid plus public USGS ScienceBase GeoDAWN release DOI 10.5066/P93LGLVQ; no new external file required.

hypotheses.name: Potential-field curvature and junctions at transfer zones
hypotheses.signature: Hessian-eigenvalue / signed-curvature ridges and cross-field junctions, evaluated at fixed metric scales and tested for continuation persistence.
hypotheses.why_unmapped: Buried fault tips, bends and transfer zones can produce localized density/magnetization curvature without a surface trace captured by existing maps.
hypotheses.difference_from_repo: Current detectors use horizontal-gradient magnitude, fixed-scale ridge and continuation persistence; no Hessian-curvature skeleton or junction detector is implemented.
hypotheses.data_availability: Current owner-mirror potential fields; no new external file.

hypotheses.name: Paleothermal-deposit corridors as fossil fault evidence
hypotheses.signature: Distance-decayed sinter/tufa/travertine support and alignment with persistent potential-field worms, assessed away from mapped traces.
hypotheses.why_unmapped: Fossil hydrothermal deposits may preserve evidence of former fluid pathways where modern fault traces are buried, eroded or unmapped.
hypotheses.difference_from_repo: B2 used 2 m temperature probes, not fossil deposit geometry; no paleothermal overlay exists in this repo.
hypotheses.data_availability: Official GDR 1391 page lists the free 82.04 kB Paleo Geothermal Features ZIP under CC BY 4.0, but direct binary retrieval returned SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL in this sandbox. Not viable here until an accessible, hash-pinned copy is obtained.

selection.reason: Highest planning-value / cost among candidates with local inputs and a directly testable structural–permeability mechanism; H29-3 remains next and is not abandoned.
